# Security review: env-driven mTLS for Temporal connections

## V1 Fail-open
- No config combination silently downgrades an intended mTLS connect:
  - `tls_from_vars` (rust/worker/src/tls.rs) folds empty/whitespace values into "unset" (`setting` closure), so `VAR= cargo run` cannot enable TLS with an empty path, and cannot pass an empty path through either.
  - Any of CERT/KEY/CA set requires all three (`missing` check → `Err` naming the missing vars); SERVER_NAME alone → `Err`. All of these abort startup via `?` in all three mains — hard fail, no fallback.
  - `require_https` closes the "TLS vars set + `http://` addr" hole: called in driver.rs:main, spike worker.rs:main, worker/bin/worker.rs:main before `Connection::connect`. Default addr (`http://127.0.0.1:7233`) with TLS set is refused (fails closed, correct direction).
- Residual (INFO, by design): no TLS vars + `https://` addr → `maybe_tls_options(None)` → SDK connects without TLS to whatever the URL says. This is the documented "unset = unchanged plain connect" contract, so not a regression, but be aware an https URL alone does not opt in.
- Cosmetic: the `require_https` error string contains a run of stray spaces ("URL;              refusing") — harmless but sloppy.

## V2 Secret handling
- `read_pem` maps `fs::read` errors to `"{var}: cannot read {path}: {e}"`; `io::Error` never carries file contents. `tls_from_vars` errors carry only variable names and paths. `main`s wrap the `String` error into anyhow — no bytes anywhere in the error chain.
- No `println!`/`{:?}` of the constructed `TlsOptions`/`ClientTlsOptions` exists in any of the three mains; the options go straight into `maybe_tls_options`. Caveat for the future: `TlsOptions` holds raw `Vec<u8>` fields, so a `Debug` print of it in later code would dump the private key — worth a note in TLS.md, not a defect in this diff.
- Paths and the address appear in errors; neither is secret material.

## V3 Server verification
- `TlsOptions::builder().maybe_server_root_ca_cert(Some(ca_bytes)).maybe_domain(server_name).maybe_client_tls_options(...)` — root CA is explicitly supplied (SDK uses it instead of system roots when set), no skip-verify/insecure option is touched, and `domain` is set only when provided, defaulting to the URL host otherwise.
- Evidence supports active verification in both directions: `rust/tls-handshake-check.sh` shows (a) client cert presented and verified by `openssl s_server -Verify 1` (positive), (b) wrong CA refused, (c) wrong server name refused. Note (b)/(c) are inferred from the *absence* of "depth=0 CN = client" in the server log — sound given the positive control, but timing-sensitive (`sleep 1`, no `set -e` in the script); flakiness risk, not a verification gap.

## V4 Error paths
- No `unwrap`/`expect` in non-test code: `read_pem` maps errors, the `let (Some(..)..) else` is a documented unreachable guard, `Url::from_str(&addr)?` and anyhow `?` handle the rest.
- Path values are trimmed by `setting` before use, so `" /path/ca.pem\n"`-style env pollution works on the clean path instead of failing obscurely; whitespace-only = unset.
- Non-PEM / malformed content: `read_pem` only checks readability; a garbage cert file is caught by the SDK at handshake time, i.e. connect failure at startup — fail-closed, acceptable (a validation-time parse would only improve the error message).

## V5 Wiring
- All three `Connection::connect` call sites in the diff use the identical pattern `tls_from_env → require_https → maybe_tls_options(tls)`: `rust/spikes/temporal-spike/src/bin/driver.rs`, `rust/spikes/temporal-spike/src/bin/worker.rs`, `rust/worker/src/bin/worker.rs`; `pub mod tls` registered in both `lib.rs` files. No plaintext `Connection::connect` remains visible in the reviewed material; I can only confirm the binaries shown — anything outside this diff wasn't provided.
- Structural concern: `spikes/temporal-spike/src/tls.rs` is a byte-identical copy of `worker/src/tls.rs`. Duplicated security code drifts; the spike tolerates it, but a shared crate would be better.

## V6 Test quality
- **Vacuous assertion (the real defect):** `missing_file_names_var_and_path` asserts `!err.contains("SECRET-KEY-MARKER")`, but `KEY_PEM` is `"-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nkey\n..."` — the marker string is never in any fixture, so the leak check can never fail regardless of behavior. It claims to pin "errors never echo key bytes" and pins nothing. Fix: put a unique marker inside `KEY_PEM` (or assert `!err.contains("BEGIN PRIVATE KEY")` and `!err.contains("key\n")`).
- Evidence mismatch: the claim says "7 unit tests per crate", the diff contains 10 `#[test]` fns in tls.rs. Either the report is stale or something differs from the shown material — worth reconciling before merging.
- Otherwise tests are meaningful: refusal rules are pinned directly (cert alone, cert+key without CA, server-name alone, each checking the named missing vars in the error), `full_set_builds_tls_options` asserts field-for-field wiring into `TlsOptions`/`ClientTlsOptions`, whitespace-in `empty_values_count_as_unset` covers trimming, and `require_https` is covered for https/HTTPS/http-with-TLS/http-without-TLS.
- Missing coverage (minor): no test for https URL with TLS unset (V1's documented-by-design case), and no test that a successfully-read file's contents stay out of other errors.

TEST-GAMING: yes - missing_file_names_var_and_path asserts absence of "SECRET-KEY-MARKER" which never appears in any test fixture, so the key-leak assertion is vacuous and passes unconditionally
VERDICT: fix - V6: make the leak assertion non-vacuous (embed a marker in KEY_PEM); reconcile the 7-vs-10 test-count claim; optionally share tls.rs instead of byte-copying it
